Let them come together to the house of our grief, and let us pour out rivers of tears with equal eyes, for our cause and our faith are one concern.

I want no heretic to come and grieve with me, who perhaps longs to add to the pain of my wounds and every day rejoices in my misfortunes. I do not, I do not want a stranger's affection; I seek a brother's. I do not want that of foreign children, whose mouth has spoken vanity and whose right hand is a right hand of iniquity; for foreign children have always lied to me, who have grown old and gone lame from their paths. Every day they say to me, "Where is your God?" while the people purchased with the precious blood of the Lamb is afflicted. Amid their taunts, ready for the scourge, I do not cease to sing to the Lord who scourges: Remove your scourges from me, for I have fainted, not from the strength of your hand, but from the persecution of the Arian heresy.

Let all come who travel the narrow way with me and, for the sake of the words of God's lips, keep to hard ways, and let them see whether there is any sorrow like my sorrow, for I have been stripped like a vineyard in the day of the Lord's fury. All my enemies have opened their mouths against me; they hissed and gnashed their teeth; they said: We have devoured her; this is the day we were waiting for; we have found it, we have seen it.

Draw near, angels of my God, who never fail in the ministry appointed to you for the sake of those who are to inherit eternal salvation, and see all Africa: once supported by the ranks of so many churches, now desolate of them all; once adorned with so many orders of priests, now sitting a widow and cast aside. Her priests and elders have perished in desert places and on islands, seeking food to eat, and they find none. Consider and see that Zion, the city of our God, has become vile; among her enemies she has become like a woman defiled by her menstruation. The enemy has laid his hand on all her precious things, for she has seen the nations invade and enter her courts, those whom you had forbidden to enter your church. Her roads mourn, because no one comes to the feast.

All her beauty and delight have departed from her face. Her virgins and young men, brought up in the halls of monasteries, have learned to walk rough roads; they have gone into captivity among the Moors, while her holy stones are scattered not only at the head of every street but also in the squalid places of the mines. Speak to our God, her protector, with confidence in your supplication, for she is in distress, and her belly is troubled with weeping, because she sits among the nations and finds no rest, and there is no one to comfort her. She looked to the regions of the East for someone to grieve with her, and there was none, and for someone to comfort her, and she found none, while she ate gall for her food and in her thirst was given vinegar to drink, imitating the sufferings of her Bridegroom and Lord, who suffered for her precisely so that she might follow in his footsteps.

(V, 20) Intercede, you patriarchs, from whose stock she was born who now labours on earth; pray, you holy prophets, recognizing in her affliction the one of whom you once sang in your prophetic proclamation; be her advocates, you apostles, who, to gather her together, ran over the whole world like the swiftest horses, with the Lord riding upon you. Above all you, blessed Peter: why are you silent about the sheep and lambs entrusted to you by our common Lord with such great care and concern? You, holy Paul, teacher of the Gentiles, who preached the gospel of God from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum, see what the Arian Vandals are doing, and how your children groan, mourning in captivity. All you holy apostles together, groan for us.

But we know that we are unworthy of your prayers, because the things that have come upon us to test us were punishments owed not to saints but to wicked deserts. Yet pray now even for wicked children, for Christ too prayed even for his enemies the Jews. Let what has justly been inflicted on us suffice for our chastisement, and now at last let pardon be asked for sinners; let it be said to the striking angel: It is enough; now hold back your hand. Who does not know that the crimes of our shameful deeds brought these things upon us, as we strayed from God's commandments and would not walk in his law? But, lying prostrate, we beg you not to spurn your wretched sinners, by him who raised you, humble fishermen, to the height of apostleship.

(V, 21) [The most wicked Huneric held the rule of the kingdom for seven years and ten months, and ended it with a death fit for his deserts. He rotted and seethed with worms, so that it was not his body but pieces of his body that seem to have been buried. And that transgressor of the law he had been given, one Nicasius, who had come over to them from the Donatist heresy, perished soon afterwards by a similar death.]
